architectural_implications.after: A model reads the declaration, decides the execution steps, and self-checks against the contract; semantics are enforced probabilistically
architectural_implications.before: A DSL requires a parser, an AST, and an executor service; semantics are enforced statically and failures are deterministic
architectural_implications.consequence: You lose static guarantees and gain zero-infrastructure iteration; testing effort shifts from parser conformance to behavioral conformance and hallucination measurement
architectural_implications.observation: The compiler/runtime is a prompt rather than a program

architectural_implications.after: Agent invoked by webhook/cron/issue event; each run is a stateless job with declared inputs and outputs
architectural_implications.before: Agent invoked by a human in a conversation; context and state scoped to the session
architectural_implications.consequence: Agents become auditable job runners that fit CI/CD and enterprise automation, but require idempotency, retry, and duplicate-event handling that chat never needed
architectural_implications.observation: Workflow entrypoint moves from chat to events

architectural_implications.after: New automation means a markdown file reviewed as text and run through the already-approved gateway
architectural_implications.before: New automation means new code, new deploy, and security/procurement review of a new artifact
architectural_implications.consequence: Shipping cost drops to documentation review cost; governance must instead track document versions and who may edit executable text
architectural_implications.observation: Agent logic is delivered as a document instead of a deployment

architectural_implications.after: The contract declares the ideal end state and the run is benchmarked against it in the same loop
architectural_implications.before: Spec lives in a design doc; evaluation lives in a separate harness with its own rubric that drifts
architectural_implications.consequence: Fewer desynchronized artifacts, but the contract's wording now directly determines both generation and grading, so a bad contract silently produces confidently wrong scores
architectural_implications.observation: Specification and evaluation become the same artifact

article_ideas.angle: Frame it as a straight swap of guarantees: what the interpreter pipeline used to give you, what you now buy instead, and the exact test artifacts a team must build before the trade pays off.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and platform architects building agent orchestration
article_ideas.thesis: For declarative agent workflows, an LLM acting as compiler and runtime is a defensible engineering trade only if you replace the parser test suite with a behavioral conformance suite; teams that adopt the first half without the second get non-deterministic failures with no static signal.
article_ideas.title: Your Compiler Should Be a Document: The Case for Trading Static Guarantees for Zero-Infrastructure Agent Runtimes

article_ideas.angle: Argue for split evaluation: the contract stays the generation target, but grading requires an independently authored rubric or a second evaluator agent, and ambiguous-contract divergence should be measured explicitly.
article_ideas.audience: Eval and reliability engineers, model-risk reviewers
article_ideas.based_on: It merges specification and evaluation into one artifact
article_ideas.thesis: Collapsing specification and evaluation into one artifact is efficient but creates a circular reasoning risk, because the wording that makes an ambiguous contract under-specified is the same wording used to certify the resulting output as correct.
article_ideas.title: The Contract That Grades Itself: Hidden Circularity in Declarative Agent Evaluation

article_ideas.angle: Walk through a single webhook-triggered agent job and enumerate everything a prose trigger declaration fails to specify, then show what must be enforced downstream of the declaration.
article_ideas.audience: Enterprise integration and platform engineers in regulated industries
article_ideas.based_on: Agents become auditable job runners that fit CI/CD
article_ideas.thesis: Choosing event triggers over conversational sessions is the right integration call, but it silently imports distributed-systems obligations, namely idempotency, retry bounds, and duplicate suppression, that chat-first agent designs never had to pay.
article_ideas.title: Finance Runs on Events, Not Chats: What Unattended Agents Owe Their Event Bus

article_ideas.angle: Separate the procurement claim from the change-management claim and show which one survives an audit and which merely relabels the artifact.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders and compliance stakeholders in finance
article_ideas.based_on: Treat agent logic as configuration/data under existing controls
article_ideas.thesis: Keeping agent logic as text under existing controls genuinely lowers shipping friction, but it moves the governance burden from procurement to document change control, so the savings are real only for organizations that already have prose review and regression discipline.
article_ideas.title: Ship the Document, Not the Deployment: Where Compliance Cost Actually Goes

connections.concept: LLM-as-compiler (prompt runtime executed by markdown readers)
connections.relationship: Replaces the mechanical stages with model interpretation; static guarantees are traded for zero infra and natural-language authoring.
The contract supplies both the generation objective and the scoring rubric, collapsing spec and eval into one artifact.

connections.connects_to: CI/CD job execution and enterprise integration
connections.relationship: Makes agents first-class automated jobs rather than interactive sessions, reusing existing event transports and approval boundaries.
Turns a periodic, labor-intensive documentation obligation into a repeatable agent run, so doc and implementation stop drifting apart.

connections.concept: Sub-agent markdown files with declared inputs/outputs
connections.connects_to: module boundaries and interface contracts in software design
connections.relationship: Establishes the file as the composition unit, enabling review, reuse, and versioning without a linker or runtime assembly step.

evidence_quotes.text: You are the compiler. This is not an analogy.
The entire agent framework is just Markdown. No parser. No binary. No SDK.
It acts as a programming language for agents, where the compiler is also just a prompt.

core_insights.generalization: Any DSL whose semantics are simple enough can be executed by an LLM instead of a bespoke interpreter, trading determinism and static checking for zero infrastructure cost and natural-language editability.
core_insights.insight: The runtime/compiler for an agent workflow is itself an LLM prompt: markdown contracts are interpreted directly by a model acting as compiler and runtime, with no parser, binary, or SDK in the loop. This collapses the traditional interpreter boundary (grammar → AST → executor) into a single model call that both validates and executes the declaration.
core_insights.why_it_matters: It removes an entire layer of infrastructure (parser, orchestration backend, deployment) and relocates correctness responsibility to the model's instruction-following. That changes what you must test: instead of parser unit tests you need prompt-runtime conformance and hallucination bounds.

evidence_quotes.text: Contracts benchmark agent output against declared ideal states to reduce hallucination loops.
Users declare what they want (the contract and end state) rather than how to do it step-by-step.

core_insights.generalization: Write specs as machine-checkable acceptance criteria co-located with intent, so generation and verification share a single source of truth.
core_insights.insight: Declarative contracts — declaring the end state and success criteria rather than a step sequence — let the harness and the model select the execution path. The contract doubles as the evaluation target: agent output is benchmarked against the declared ideal state, which the speakers claim reduces hallucination loops.
core_insights.why_it_matters: It merges specification and evaluation into one artifact, so the same text that generates the run also gates it. This is a cheap evaluator-optimizer loop that doesn't require a separate rubric-maintenance pipeline.

evidence_quotes.text: Finance runs on events, not chats.
Workflows are event-driven, triggering automatically when external events happen.
A GitHub issue opening or a scheduled cron job triggering an agent execution.

core_insights.generalization: Design agents as event consumers with declared input/output contracts, not as always-on conversational services; the integration surface becomes the event bus rather than a UI.
core_insights.insight: The trigger layer is event-driven (webhooks, GitHub issue opens, cron), not conversational. Workflows fire from external system events and produce automated job output, deliberately avoiding chat interfaces.
core_insights.why_it_matters: Chat-first agent designs couple the agent to a human-in-the-loop session and to session-scoped context. Event-triggered execution makes agents CI/CD citizens — deterministic entrypoints, no interactive state — and is what lets them slot into existing enterprise infrastructure without new procurement.

evidence_quotes.text: Regulated finance companies don't need procurement or IT departments because OpenProse is entirely text.
Using existing approved LLM gateways and coding agents without changing security controls.

core_insights.generalization: Treat agent logic as configuration/data under existing controls rather than as new software, and deployment friction drops to the cost of a document review.
core_insights.insight: Because the program is plain text, it inherits the organization's existing compliance and security perimeter: it runs through already-approved LLM gateways and coding agents, so no new procurement or IT review is required for each new workflow.
core_insights.why_it_matters: In regulated environments, approval overhead — not engineering effort — is the dominant cost of shipping a new automation. Keeping logic as data (markdown) rather than as a deployable artifact changes the governance path fundamentally.

evidence_quotes.text: Standard operating procedures and quant model documentation can be executed directly as prose programs.
Discussion of quantitative models in big banks requiring annual re-documentation.

core_insights.generalization: Where a written procedure already exists and is authoritative, the highest-leverage agent workload is executing that procedure and regenerating the document from the run, not authoring a separate pipeline.
core_insights.insight: Institutional operating knowledge — SOPs and quant-model methodology docs that must be re-documented annually — is proposed as directly executable prose programs, with generation of methodology documentation (e.g., USD OIS discount curves) as the demonstrated workload.
core_insights.why_it_matters: It reframes documentation as an executable artifact rather than a stale parallel description. If a doc is the program, doc drift and implementation drift collapse into one failure mode instead of two.

evidence_quotes.text: OpenProse allows writing prompts compositionally using declarative contracts.
Writing markdown files to manage multi-agent workflows without deploying new code stacks.

core_insights.generalization: Pick a text-native module boundary with explicit declared inputs/outputs so agents can be composed and reviewed by the same process as code, without a runtime linking step.
core_insights.insight: Composition is achieved by file-level decomposition — sub-agents, skills, tools, inputs, outputs, triggers — declared in separate markdown files rather than wired in code, allowing prompts to be composed like modules.
core_insights.why_it_matters: Defines a concrete composition unit (the markdown file with declared I/O) that can be reviewed, versioned, and reused, which is the missing primitive in most prompt-reuse schemes.

evidence_quotes.text: The entire agent framework is just markdown with no parser, binary, or SDK required.
It acts as a programming language for agents, where the compiler is also just a prompt.

deep_dives.research_question: If the runtime and compiler of a markdown agent workflow are themselves prompts, what test suite replaces parser unit tests, and how much cross-run and cross-model variance does a fixed contract exhibit?
deep_dives.topic: Behavioral conformance testing for an LLM-as-compiler runtime
deep_dives.trigger_insight: The runtime/compiler for an agent workflow is itself an LLM prompt
deep_dives.why: Removing the parser moves correctness responsibility onto instruction-following, so the failure surface shifts from syntax errors to silent interpretation drift. Without a conformance harness you cannot tell whether a contract edit or a model version bump changed behavior, which makes the whole architecture unauditable in practice.

evidence_quotes.text: declaring intent, contracts, and outcomes in plain markdown—rather than writing imperative Python or complex orchestration code—allows intelligent agents to figure out the 'how'
It bridges the gap between business requirements and technical execution using human-readable contracts.

deep_dives.research_question: When the contract supplies both the generation objective and the scoring rubric, does the contract-grader reproduce the generator's misinterpretations, and does a second independent evaluator agent catch what the first certifies as correct?
deep_dives.topic: Self-grading contracts: circularity between generation target and evaluation rubric
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Contracts benchmark agent output against declared ideal states
deep_dives.why: The claim that contracts benchmark output against declared ideal states to reduce hallucination loops is asserted without error rates. If the same wording drives generation and grading, an ambiguous contract yields confidently wrong passes, which is worse than a loud failure because it produces no signal to act on.

evidence_quotes.text: Workflows are event-driven, triggering automatically when external events happen.
It avoids conversational chat interfaces in favor of automated job execution.
A GitHub issue opening or a scheduled cron job triggering an agent execution.

deep_dives.research_question: What minimal job semantics (idempotency keys, retry policy, duplicate-event suppression, dead-letter handling) must a markdown-declared event-driven agent carry before it can safely run unattended against enterprise event sources?
deep_dives.topic: Event-triggered agent jobs need idempotency, retry, and duplicate-event semantics that chat never required
deep_dives.trigger_insight: The trigger layer is event-driven (webhooks, GitHub issue opens, cron), not conversational
deep_dives.why: Moving the entrypoint from a human conversation to a webhook or cron job converts each run into a stateless automated job. Chat scoped state hid exactly the problems that now become production incidents: replayed events, partial writes, and unbounded retry loops, none of which a prose trigger declaration expresses by default.

evidence_quotes.text: Regulated finance companies don't need procurement or IT departments because OpenProse is entirely text.
Using existing approved LLM gateways and coding agents without changing security controls.
If you can read logical English, you can read and edit the contract.

deep_dives.research_question: How do version control, review, and rollback work when the program, the runtime contract, and the compiler instruction are all natural-language documents editable by non-engineers under an existing compliance perimeter?
deep_dives.topic: Governance of executable prose: provenance, diff review, and rollback for programs that are documents
deep_dives.trigger_insight: it inherits the organization's existing compliance and security perimeter
deep_dives.why: The compliance argument rests on the logic being text that flows through already-approved gateways rather than a new deployable artifact. That only holds if change control moves with it: document versioning, reviewer identity, golden-run regression per revision, and pinned model versions. Otherwise the governance path was relabeled, not shortened.

evidence_quotes.text: OpenProse allows writing prompts compositionally using declarative contracts.
Writing markdown files to manage multi-agent workflows without deploying new code stacks.

deep_dives.research_question: What file granularity and declared input/output schema minimize interface mismatch and review effort when workflows are composed from many sub-agent markdown files, given that nothing statically checks the interfaces?
deep_dives.topic: File-level module boundaries for composed sub-agents and interface validation without a linker
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Composition is achieved by file-level decomposition
deep_dives.why: The file is proposed as the composition unit, but with no runtime assembly step there is no linker to catch a mismatch between one file's declared output and another's declared input. Boundary conventions and a lightweight interface check are what make prompt reuse safe rather than aspirational.

open_questions.why_unresolved: A business-impact figure is asserted with no methodology, customer, or audit outcome evidence in the summary.

open_questions.question: How do you observe and version control a system whose program, runtime, and compiler are all natural-language documents under continuous editing by non-engineers?
open_questions.research_direction: Adapt code-review and CI practices to prose repos: diff-based review, golden-run regression tests per contract, and pinned model versions per contract revision.
open_questions.why_unresolved: The architecture moves logic to text without specifying provenance, change review, or rollback semantics.

project_ideas.based_on: instead of parser unit tests you need prompt-runtime conformance and hallucination bounds
project_ideas.hypothesis: A fixed set of markdown contracts executed N times across M model versions will show run-to-run output variance concentrated in contracts with implicit success criteria, and explicit acceptance criteria co-located in the contract will measurably reduce that variance.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-contract output divergence rate across runs, pass rate against declared criteria, retry count, and token cost per successful run; compare explicit-criteria versus prose-only cohorts.
project_ideas.name: Contract Conformance Bench
project_ideas.poc: Build 12 contracts (half with explicit machine-checkable acceptance criteria, half with prose-only intent), run each 20 times across two model versions through the same gateway, and diff normalized outputs plus declared-criteria pass rates.

project_ideas.based_on: whether a second independent evaluator agent catches what the first misses
project_ideas.hypothesis: Deliberately ambiguous contracts will be silently resolved to a single interpretation that the contract-based grader then certifies as correct, and an independently authored second evaluator will flag a detectable share of those self-certified passes.
project_ideas.measurement: Percentage of ambiguous contracts where grader passes output judged wrong by human adjudication, and the recall of the independent evaluator on that subset.
project_ideas.name: Ambiguity Divergence Probe
project_ideas.poc: Author 10 contracts with one planted ambiguity each, run generation plus contract-as-grader, then run an independent evaluator with no access to the generator's reasoning; manually adjudicate disagreements.

project_ideas.based_on: require idempotency, retry, and duplicate-event handling that chat never needed
project_ideas.hypothesis: An event-triggered markdown-declared agent job without idempotency keys and duplicate-event suppression will produce duplicate side effects on replayed webhooks at a rate above zero, and adding a declared job-identity layer will drive that to zero without changing the contract prose.
project_ideas.measurement: Duplicate side effects per 100 replayed events, retry loop depth, recovery time after injected mid-run failure, and contract-diff size required to gain the guarantee.
project_ideas.name: Idempotent Event-Trigger Runner
project_ideas.poc: Wrap a contract-declared workflow in a thin event adapter that replays the same webhook and cron events with injected duplicates and partial failures, first naive, then with idempotency keys and a dead-letter path.

project_ideas.based_on: doc drift and implementation drift collapse into one failure mode
project_ideas.hypothesis: Where a written procedure is the authoritative source, executing the procedure document and regenerating the documentation from the run will surface latent discrepancies between the prose and actual execution that a human re-documentation pass misses.
project_ideas.measurement: Number and severity of semantic discrepancies found per document, reviewer acceptance score of the regenerated document, and edit volume required before sign-off.
project_ideas.name: Executable SOP Drift Detector
project_ideas.poc: Take two internal SOPs and one methodology-style document, run each as an executable prose program, auto-regenerate the document from the run trace, and diff against the human-authored version.

summary.html:
Overview

  • Speaker: Dan Barrett, Raymond Weitekamp, Jose Montes de Oca
  • Channel: AI Engineer
  • Main topic: Event-Based Multi-Agent Financial Workflows with Only Markdown
  • Purpose: To demonstrate how OpenProse enables event-driven multi-agent workflows using pure markdown contracts and declarations. This workshop introduces OpenProse, a framework and language for agent-based multi-agent workflows written entirely in markdown. The speakers explain how declaring intent, contracts, and outcomes in plain markdown—rather than writing imperative Python or complex orchestration code—allows intelligent agents to figure out the 'how', dramatically simplifying multi-agent composition and integration with existing enterprise stacks.

Topic Map

Introduction to OpenProse and Markdown Workflows

  • Explanation: Dan Barrett and Raymond Weitekamp introduce OpenProse, explaining why programming language models with markdown is powerful and how intent is communicated to super-intelligence.
  • Key claims:
    • Language is the most powerful force of creation.
    • You can write a sentence and make that sentence true.
    • OpenProse allows writing prompts compositionally using declarative contracts.
  • Examples:
    • Writing markdown files to manage multi-agent workflows without deploying new code stacks.
  • Terminology:
    • OpenProse
    • Prompt composition
    • Contract creation
    • Declarative prompting
  • Why it matters: It allows developers to compose complex agent workflows using only text documents, lowering friction and infrastructure overhead.

Just Markdown & Event-Driven Architecture

  • Explanation: Raymond Weitekamp explains the two core pillars of OpenProse: it is entirely markdown, and it operates in an event-driven manner rather than conversational chat.
  • Key claims:
    • The entire agent framework is just markdown with no parser, binary, or SDK required.
    • Workflows are event-driven, triggering automatically when external events happen.
    • It avoids conversational chat interfaces in favor of automated job execution.
  • Examples:
    • A GitHub issue opening or a scheduled cron job triggering an agent execution.
  • Terminology:
    • Event-driven workflows
    • Markdown framework
    • Webhooks
    • Cron jobs
  • Why it matters: It integrates seamlessly with existing enterprise systems and CI/CD pipelines via plain text.

Why Should I Care? (Benefits for Finance, Developers, and PMs)

  • Explanation: Breaking down the benefits for regulated finance industries, AI engineers, and non-coding product managers.
  • Key claims:
    • Regulated finance companies don't need procurement or IT departments because OpenProse is entirely text.
    • If you can read logical English, you can read and edit the contract.
    • It acts as a programming language for agents, where the compiler is also just a prompt.
  • Examples:
    • Using existing approved LLM gateways and coding agents without changing security controls.
  • Terminology:
    • Guardrails
    • Logical English
    • Multi-agent workflows
    • Compliance
  • Why it matters: It bridges the gap between business requirements and technical execution using human-readable contracts.

Live Demos: run.prose.md and GitHub PR Reviews

  • Explanation: Demonstrating practical execution of OpenProse programs using GitHub webhooks, pull request reviews, and financial methodology documentation.
  • Key claims:
    • You can use run.prose.md to develop and maintain prose repositories.
    • Agents can act as grumpy senior developers reviewing pull requests.
    • Contracts benchmark agent output against declared ideal states to reduce hallucination loops.
  • Examples:
    • Automated pull request review workflows checking code against methodology documents.
  • Terminology:
    • Prose right function
    • Sub-agents
    • Evaluator-optimizer loop
    • Kernel
  • Why it matters: Shows real-world utility in software engineering and financial auditing tasks.

Key Points

Agents as Compilers

  • Explanation: The runtime and compiler in OpenProse are themselves LLM prompts where markdown code gets interpreted and compiled into execution.
  • Evidence: Raymond Weitekamp stating 'You are the compiler. This is not an analogy.'
  • Practical implication: Reduces the need for traditional software parsers and heavy backend orchestration frameworks.

Declarative vs. Imperative Prompting

  • Explanation: Users declare what they want (the contract and end state) rather than how to do it step-by-step.
  • Evidence: Explaining that the harness and intelligent model will figure out the execution steps.
  • Practical implication: Lowers cost and leverages smarter models to figure out optimal execution paths.

Institutional Operational Knowledge as Markdown

  • Explanation: Standard operating procedures and quant model documentation can be executed directly as prose programs.
  • Evidence: Discussion of quantitative models in big banks requiring annual re-documentation.
  • Practical implication: Saves millions of dollars in compliance and auditing overhead by turning SOPs into executable agent specifications.

Frameworks, Models & Processes

OpenProse

  • How it works: A markdown-based framework where events trigger agent execution against declarative contracts defined in text files.
  • Components:
    • Sub-agents
    • Skills
    • Tools
    • Inputs
    • Outputs
    • Triggers
  • When to use: When building reliable, repeatable, auditable multi-agent workflows without traditional coding frameworks.

Examples & Case Studies

An AGI-filled junior pull request review job triggered by a GitHub webhook.

  • Illustrates: Event-driven execution of markdown contracts.
  • Lesson: Agents can autonomously review code against strict guidelines and output structured suggestions.

Generating methodology documentation for USD OIS discount curves.

  • Illustrates: Handling complex financial and quant model documentation.
  • Lesson: OpenProse can automate expensive regulatory and compliance documentation workflows.

Actionable Takeaways

  • Immediate:
    • Try out OpenProse locally using npm skills add openprose/prose.
    • Explore run.prose.md for hosted event-driven workflows.
  • Strategic:
    • Shift from imperative agent orchestration graphs to declarative markdown contracts.
    • Leverage existing enterprise security stacks by keeping agent logic as plain text documents.
  • Questions to investigate:
    • How does OpenProse handle token efficiency at scale for massive multi-agent pipelines?
    • What are the best practices for structuring composable sub-agent markdown files?

Claims Worth Verifying

  • OpenProse requires no parser, binary, or SDK, running purely on markdown text. (technical architecture)
  • Financial institutions save between $10M to $50M a year on quant model re-documentation using automated workflows. (business impact)

Notable Quotes

"The entire agent framework is just Markdown. No parser. No binary. No SDK." "Finance runs on events, not chats." "You are the compiler. This is not an analogy. You are the compiler, and it seems to work."

Compressed Summary

  • OpenProse is a markdown-based framework for event-driven multi-agent workflows.
  • Workflows are declarative contracts defining goals, inputs, outputs, and sub-agents.
  • Integrates with existing webhooks, cron jobs, and LLM coding agents without custom software infrastructure.
  • Highly applicable for regulated finance, compliance auditing, and automated code reviews.
  • Keywords: openprose, markdown, agents, event-driven, orchestration, finance
  • Core insight: OpenProse replaces complex imperative agent frameworks with declarative markdown contracts, allowing event-driven multi-agent workflows to be read, edited, and composed entirely as plain text.

## Key Points
### Agents as Compilers
- **Explanation**: The runtime and compiler in OpenProse are themselves LLM prompts where markdown code gets interpreted and compiled into execution.
- **Evidence**: Raymond Weitekamp stating 'You are the compiler. This is not an analogy.'
- **Practical implication**: Reduces the need for traditional software parsers and heavy backend orchestration frameworks.
### Declarative vs. Imperative Prompting
- **Explanation**: Users declare what they want (the contract and end state) rather than how to do it step-by-step.
- **Evidence**: Explaining that the harness and intelligent model will figure out the execution steps.
- **Practical implication**: Lowers cost and leverages smarter models to figure out optimal execution paths.
### Institutional Operational Knowledge as Markdown
- **Explanation**: Standard operating procedures and quant model documentation can be executed directly as prose programs.
- **Evidence**: Discussion of quantitative models in big banks requiring annual re-documentation.
- **Practical implication**: Saves millions of dollars in compliance and auditing overhead by turning SOPs into executable agent specifications.
